newsitem.title: USA: RESEARCH ALERT - General Mills rating cut.
newsitem.headline: RESEARCH ALERT - General Mills rating cut.

text.p: -- Goldman Sachs analyst Nomi Ghez said Wednesday she cut her rating on food company General Mills Inc to market perform from outperform.
-- She lowered her earnings estimate for General Mills, the number two U.S. cereal market, to $3.05 a share from $3.10 for fiscal 1997 and to $3.40 from $3.50 for fiscal 1998.
-- General Mills shares were off 1-3/4 at 63.
-- Ghez said she lowered her rating and earnings estimates based on "below-expectation cereal volume for General Mills and below-expectation growth for the category."
-- "The (cereal) category is just not picking up," Ghez said.
-- Earlier, General Mills reported earnings for the third quarter ended February 23 of $0.78 a share, in line with estimates, up from $0.73 a year ago.

-- Its domestic retail packaged food volume dropped one percent in the quarter, cereal volume declined three percent in the quarter. For the year-to-date period, General Mills' domestic cereal volume was up four percent, outpacing the ready-to-eat cereal category's one percent growth.
